topRisks: CRITICAL · NOI quality / manufactured NOI — ~$67,527/yr of NOI overstated → ≈$1,286,229 of value at 5.3%.
CRITICAL · Occupancy & leased-rate integrity — ~$782,059/yr NOI exposure if leased rate holds (≈$14,896,370 of value at 5.3%).
CRITICAL · Capital-expenditure & reserve adequacy — Reserve shortfall ~$24,634/yr (≈$469,219 of value); interior renovation est. $1.5–2.5M unfunded.
HIGH · Missing due-diligence coverage — Screening rests on marketing figures until DD is received.
HIGH · Year-1 rent-growth aggressiveness — ~$264,465 of Year-1 revenue not yet in place.

flags.evidence: Seller Year-1 NOI ($6,911,304) exceeds T-12 actual ($6,859,742) via expense cuts, not revenue: Turnover -32.1% and R&M -25.7% below T-12.
flags.whyItMatters: NOI lifted by cutting expenses below trailing actuals — rather than growing revenue — is not durable. It is the single most common OM overstatement and directly inflates value at the going-in cap.
flags.financialImpact: ~$67,527/yr of NOI overstated → ≈$1,286,229 of value at 5.3%.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Re-underwrite controllable expenses to T-12 actuals; treat 'market adjustments' as unproven until third-party bids support them.

flags.evidence: 96.0% occupied but only 85.0% leased — a 11-pt gap (~24 units under notice) vs an underwritten 5.0% vacancy.
flags.whyItMatters: Physical occupancy counts bodies in units; leased rate counts signed leases net of notices. A large leased-below-occupied gap signals a forward vacancy wave that the seller's underwritten vacancy does not capture.
flags.financialImpact: ~$782,059/yr NOI exposure if leased rate holds (≈$14,896,370 of value at 5.3%).
flags.recommendedNextAction: Pull the notice-to-vacate report and 60-day leasing velocity; re-underwrite vacancy to the leased rate until velocity proves otherwise.

flags.evidence: Reserves only $137/unit for a 2015 12-story asset; the marketed value-add thesis carries $0 of renovation capital.
flags.whyItMatters: Thin reserves plus a value-add thesis with zero renovation capital means the upside is claimed but unfunded — the buyer pays for NOI growth that requires unbudgeted capital to achieve.
flags.financialImpact: Reserve shortfall ~$24,634/yr (≈$469,219 of value); interior renovation est. $1.5–2.5M unfunded.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Budget interior + fitness-center capital and raise reserves to ≥$250/unit for a 12-story asset; net the capital from the bid.

flags.evidence: 8 critical DD items not provided in the OM: Full unit-level rent roll, T-12 operating statement + GL, Leased-vs-occupied / NTV report, Bound insurance policy + loss runs, …
flags.whyItMatters: Core underwriting inputs absent from the OM mean the screening rests on marketing figures; the deal cannot clear IC until they are obtained.
flags.financialImpact: Screening rests on marketing figures until DD is received.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Issue the DD request list; do not advance to IC until the rent roll, T-12 statement, leases, and PCA are received.

flags.evidence: Seller underwrites +3.5% Year-1 rent growth off the T-3, yet T-12 GSR ($7,601,310) exceeds T-3 annualized ($7,556,129) — rents are decelerating, not accelerating.
flags.whyItMatters: Front-loaded rent growth inflates Year-1 NOI and therefore going-in value. It is only credible with signed-lease trade-out evidence, especially when trailing rents are flat-to-down.
flags.financialImpact: ~$264,465 of Year-1 revenue not yet in place.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Require signed new-lease and renewal trade-out data for the last 6 months before crediting Year-1 growth.

flags.evidence: Insurance underwritten at $139,431 vs T-12 $57,596 — a 142.1% step-change.
flags.whyItMatters: A >50% swing between trailing and underwritten insurance means either T-12 is understated (further NOI drag) or the UW is padded — either way the true run-rate is unknown without the bound policy.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Obtain the bound policy and 5-year loss runs; set insurance to the quoted renewal, not a $/unit rule of thumb.

flags.evidence: No PCA in the OM. Roof is original TPO from 2015 (~11 yrs, mid-life). Boiler replaced 2024 (mitigant).
flags.whyItMatters: A single-membrane roof and other major systems near end of service life are large, lumpy costs. Absent a PCA, they are unquantified and unreserved.
flags.financialImpact: Roof replacement est. $1.5–2.5M within a typical hold — unreserved.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Commission a Property Condition Assessment; obtain roof age/warranty and a 12-year capital plan.

flags.evidence: At 60.0% LTV / 6.3% / 30-yr, coverage is 1.41x during the 2-yr IO but only 1.19x once amortizing — below the 1.25x floor.
flags.whyItMatters: Coverage below 1.25x on a fully-amortizing basis means the asset barely services its debt once interest-only burns off — a refinancing and distribution risk.
flags.financialImpact: Post-IO coverage cushion is thin; distributions compress when the loan begins amortizing.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Size debt to a 1.25x amortizing DSCR floor; stress the post-IO coverage before committing.

flags.evidence: Seller underwrites a 2.0% management fee vs a 3.0% market benchmark; T-12 shows $0 (self-managed) — no third-party benchmark.
flags.whyItMatters: A below-market management fee understates operating cost and overstates NOI. Mixed-use high-rises with ground-floor retail warrant 2.5–3.5%.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Underwrite management to 3.0% of EGI (market for a 12-story mixed-use asset).

flags.evidence: RE taxes $786,927 = 8.1% of EGI, grown only ~3%/yr off the assessor FMV; a sale near $124,638,000 FMV plus assessment-rate changes in Metro City create reassessment exposure not modeled.
flags.whyItMatters: A sale can trigger reassessment and assessment rates change; underwriting taxes flat to the current bill understates go-forward expense.
flags.financialImpact: Each +10% to the tax bill ≈ $78,693/yr of NOI.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Model a reassessment-on-sale scenario at the purchase basis; confirm the current mill levy and assessment ratio.

flags.evidence: 5 documented inconsistencies: Framing described inconsistently between the summary and the construction detail; Physical occupancy stated well above leased rate; Comparable property unit count conflicts between two pages; ….
flags.whyItMatters: Internal contradictions in the OM undermine confidence in every extracted figure and must be reconciled before any number is trusted.
flags.financialImpact: Extraction confidence reduced; verify all figures against source docs.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Reconcile each inconsistency against the rent roll and T-12 source documents before relying on OM figures.

flags.evidence: OM markets interior-upgrade premiums on a $/unit basis with no $/SF normalization and no achieved-lease evidence; the supporting ROI detail is referenced but not included.
flags.whyItMatters: Marketed upgrade premiums ($/unit/month) mean nothing without $/SF normalization and achieved-lease evidence — unit-size mix can masquerade as renovation lift (the classic OM overstatement).
flags.financialImpact: Upgrade upside unverified — exclude from value until substantiated.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Obtain the 'ROIs & Amenities' data-room sheet; normalize premiums to $/SF against classic units of like size.

flags.evidence: Comp rent/PSF figures conflict between sections of the OM. Subject $2.94/SF vs the Central submarket average $3.28/SF.
flags.whyItMatters: Rent comps drive the mark-to-market thesis; internal inconsistencies between OM sections undermine any premium/discount conclusion.
flags.financialImpact: Mark-to-market upside cannot be sized until comps are reconciled.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Rebuild the comp set from primary source (CoStar) at like vintage/geography; reconcile the OM's conflicting figures.

flags.evidence: Retail income volatility: anchor Anchor restaurant tenant (47.7% of retail SF) has a 2026 base-rent abatement; ~20.0% of retail SF rolls within the hold.
flags.whyItMatters: Concentrated retail rollover and an anchor rent abatement create near-term income volatility that the blended pro forma masks.
flags.financialImpact: Near-term retail income at risk of re-lease downtime and TI/LC.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Abstract every retail lease; model any disclosed abatement and the retail rollover schedule explicitly.

flags.evidence: Metro City: no statewide rent control (favorable), but the OM does not affirmatively disclose the absence of affordable/income-restricted units.
flags.whyItMatters: Rent regulation and undisclosed affordable/restricted units cap upside and change the risk profile.
flags.recommendedNextAction: Confirm no affordable/income-restricted units and no local rent-stabilization overlay in the applicable jurisdiction.

insufficientData.evidence: No unit-level rent roll, no market-rent column and no stated loss-to-lease. Subject in-place $2,808 ($2.94/SF) vs a Central submarket average of $3.28/SF.
insufficientData.whyItMatters: Loss-to-lease is the gap between in-place and market rent — the core of any rent upside thesis. Without a unit-level roll and market rents it cannot be verified.
insufficientData.financialImpact: Rent-upside thesis unquantifiable from the OM.
insufficientData.recommendedNextAction: Obtain the full unit-level rent roll with market-rent column; compute LTL by unit and by floor plan.

insufficientData.evidence: OM is unpriced and free-and-clear — no asking price or going-in cap. At the assessor FMV ($124,638,000): 5.3% on re-underwritten NOI vs 5.5% on the seller's Year-1 NOI.
insufficientData.whyItMatters: An OM offered unpriced gives no going-in cap or price-per-unit anchor. Value must be triangulated from re-underwritten NOI and a cap-rate matrix, not the seller's numbers.
insufficientData.financialImpact: Each 25 bps of cap ≈ $6,296,573 of value swing at this NOI.
insufficientData.recommendedNextAction: Confirm pricing guidance; value off re-underwritten NOI via a cap-rate sensitivity matrix; do not bid to the seller's Year-1 NOI.

passes.whyItMatters: Leverage above 75% leaves a thin equity cushion against value declines.
passes.recommendedNextAction: Keep leverage ≤65–70% given the aggressive OM basis.

passes.evidence: Debt yield 8.8% on re-underwritten NOI — above the 8.0% floor.
passes.whyItMatters: Debt yield (NOI ÷ loan) is the lender's downside test; below ~8% signals aggressive proceeds relative to income.
passes.recommendedNextAction: Confirm lender debt-yield floor; size proceeds to ≥8% on re-underwritten NOI.

passes.evidence: Central submarket shows constrained supply: office vacancy 4.0%, retail 2.0%, est. MF vacancy ~2.0%; 1-mile avg HH income $210,151+; 1127 submarket units in the pipeline. No rent control disclosed.
passes.whyItMatters: Supply-constrained, high-income submarkets protect occupancy and pricing power — the demand side of the thesis. A PASS here proves the rule set discriminates rather than flagging everything.
passes.recommendedNextAction: Confirm the multifamily (not office/retail) vacancy and 2024–2028 delivery pipeline with CoStar.
